chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Haysam ibn Abi Masruq al-Nehdi, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad, from al-Hariz, from al-Zurarah said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
We are a Household whose chivalry (mar'ah) is to forgive those who have oppressed us.

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتٍ: Ahl al-Bayt (the Household, referring to the Prophet's family and Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of chivalry (mar'ah) for the Ahl al-Bayt according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies 'mar'ah' (nobility/chivalry) as the defining trait of the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically manifested through the forgiveness of those who wrong them. This concept elevates the Imams' conduct beyond mere justice to a higher spiritual station of magnanimity, serving as a model for their followers to emulate in social interactions. The narration underscores that true nobility is proven not by power, but by the grace shown to adversaries.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-33 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masruq al-Nehdi, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najran, on the authority of Himad, on the authority of Hurayz that Zurarah said, “I heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say, ‘
We are members of a Household whose chivalry is to forgive those who have oppressed us.’”
